title: AWS CWI Training in Lake Charles, LA: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Lake Charles LNG, refinery and chemical plant welders: ASME, D1.1 or API 1104 for Part C. Corporate, online or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation for Lake Charles: Six Days for LNG, Refinery and Chemical Plant Welding Inspectors
html:
Follow the Calcasieu Ship Channel south from Lake Charles toward the Gulf and you pass refineries, chemical complexes, and liquefied natural gas terminals, some already shipping cargoes and others still rising out of the marsh. Very little of that steel goes into service until a welding inspector has signed it off, and in Southwest Louisiana the qualification that owners and contractors write into their specifications most often is the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI). Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for that examination with a six-day (6-day) course built around all three parts: Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. It comes in three formats: corporate delivery at an employer's facility, online study for individuals, and one-to-one sessions with the instructor. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis prepares people for it and certifies no one.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Lake Charles. The company keeps two offices, in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India, and Calcasieu and Cameron Parish candidates take the course through the formats described below. To scope it for yourself or a crew, send a Lake Charles CWI enquiry.

How the six days work for a Lake Charles candidate

The outline never changes; only the delivery does. Days one and two cover the Part A fundamentals: welding and cutting processes, AWS terms and definitions, joint geometry, welding symbols, metallurgy, destructive tests, discontinuities and their causes, the main NDT methods, safety, fabrication math and the inspector's responsibilities. Day three rehearses the Part B practical with gauges and weld specimens. Day four is spent inside the code book you will carry into Part C. Day five is timed practice papers, and day six goes back over whatever those papers exposed, along with exam-day logistics. The AWS CWI exam prep course page sets out each day in full.

  • Corporate: an LNG contractor, refinery maintenance firm or fabrication shop with several people to prepare has the six days delivered at its own Southwest Louisiana premises, using its welds, its gauges and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online: an individual gets a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and sends questions to an instructor while working through them. There are no scheduled class times, so the pace follows your shifts and rotations.
  • One-to-one: a single candidate works through six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

Atlantis drafts its practice items itself, working from the subject lists AWS makes public. They are not real AWS examination questions, and AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

The Lake Charles welding economy, sector by sector

LNG export terminals, running and under construction

Few places build and operate LNG export plants at the pace of Southwest Louisiana. Cheniere's Sabine Pass terminal sits near the Texas line, Cameron LNG, owned by Sempra together with Mitsui, Mitsubishi and TotalEnergies, runs three liquefaction trains, and Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass terminal operates in Cameron Parish. Construction has not slowed. Venture Global began full mobilization at CP2 LNG in Cameron Parish in mid-2025 with Worley as its engineering, procurement and construction contractor, took a second phase to a final investment decision in March 2026, and is aiming for first LNG in 2027. In Calcasieu Parish, Woodside's Louisiana LNG reached full notice to proceed in May 2025, with Bechtel building the first three trains and two large storage tanks; Bechtel expects the site workforce to peak at about 5,000. Other projects, such as Commonwealth LNG and Energy Transfer's Lake Charles LNG export plan, have been moving through approvals.

For a welding inspector, an LNG build is a mixed workload. Liquefaction trains arrive as modules packed with process piping built to ASME B31.3, much of it austenitic stainless steel for cryogenic service, where qualification records often call for low-temperature impact testing and where fit-up, purging and interpass control decide whether a root pass survives volumetric examination. Pipe racks, module frames, platforms and equipment supports are structural steel, usually welded to AWS D1.1. The full-containment storage tanks typically have inner tanks of 9% nickel steel, built under API 620 and API 625 and welded with nickel-alloy consumables by specialist tank contractors. An inspector who can move between those documents, and always knows which one governs the joint in front of them, is useful on every one of these sites.

Refineries along the channel

Louisiana's refinery survey lists three refineries in the Lake Charles area: the CITGO plant, which carries a Sulphur address and is plainly visible from I-10; the Phillips 66 Lake Charles complex in Westlake; and the smaller Calcasieu Refining Company. Refinery welding is mostly maintenance and turnaround work, replacing corroded spools, nozzles and exchanger components under ASME B31.3 and the owner's engineering standards, with procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX. Chrome-moly and stainless lines put preheat, postweld heat treatment and hardness checks into the inspector's routine, and a turnaround squeezes months of that work into a few weeks.

Chemical complexes in Westlake and Lake Charles

The chemical side is just as dense. Sasol's Lake Charles Chemical Complex sits beside Westlake's Lake Charles North site, and Westlake runs four operations in the area making vinyl chloride monomer, chlor-alkali products, ethylene and polyethylene. LyondellBasell makes polypropylene, Indorama Ventures makes ethylene, Lotte Chemical Louisiana makes mono-ethylene glycol, and W.R. Grace runs a large refining catalyst plant. Corrosive and high-temperature services mean alloy piping, frequent repairs and a steady flow of small capital projects, each of which needs welding inspection against the plant's own specifications.

Pipelines and compressor stations

The terminals depend on gas arriving by pipeline. Venture Global's CP Express pipeline is being built to supply CP2, and federal regulators approved its Moss Lake Compressor Station in late 2025. Interstate gas line welding falls under the federal pipeline safety rules in 49 CFR Part 192, which incorporate API 1104 for welder qualification and weld acceptance, so spreads, tie-ins and station builds across the parishes need inspectors fluent in that standard.

The new I-10 Calcasieu River Bridge

Public works add another kind of welding. The Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development is replacing the I-10 bridge over the Calcasieu River through a public-private partnership with Calcasieu Bridge Partners, a team made up of Plenary, Acciona and Sacyr. Ground was broken in 2026, and construction is scheduled to run until mid-2031. Bridge programs bring AWS D1.5 and state shop inspection requirements wherever welded steel is part of the structure, and the approaches, ramps and relocated utilities around them create structural and piping work for local fabricators.

Who hires CWIs around Lake Charles, and what they ask for

  • EPC contractors on LNG projects. Contractors such as Bechtel and Worley staff large quality departments, and the owner specifications on those builds spell out the welding inspector qualifications expected. Experience with stainless process piping and module work counts.
  • Plant maintenance and turnaround contractors. Firms holding long-term contracts in the refineries and chemical plants keep inspectors year round and add more during outages, with ASME Section IX and B31.3 knowledge as the baseline.
  • Owner QA and inspection groups. Operators keep their own welding specialists to review the procedures, welder qualification records, weld maps and heat-treatment charts that contractors submit.
  • Pipe, module and structural fabricators. Shops supplying spools, skids and steelwork to the terminals and plants need in-house QC who can accept work before it ships.
  • Third-party inspection firms. Vendor-shop source inspection and field surveillance for owners is often done by CWIs; Atlantis describes its own work in this area on third-party inspection in Lake Charles.
  • Pipeline contractors. Spreads, tie-ins and compressor stations call for API 1104 knowledge on top of general welding inspection skills.

Which Part C code suits Lake Charles work?

Part C is the open-book code application paper, and AWS lets you choose the book. The list AWS published in November 2026 included AWS D1.1 for structural steel, API 1104 for pipelines, AWS D1.2 for aluminum, AWS D1.5 for bridges, AWS D15.1 for railcars and locomotives, AWS D17.1 for aerospace, an ASME package combining Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. In Calcasieu and Cameron parishes, four of those cover almost everyone.

Most of your work isBook to considerWhy it fits
LNG process piping, refinery and chemical plant maintenance, turnaroundsASME (Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3)It is the qualification and piping framework you already work to inside the fence.
Module frames, pipe racks, structural steel, fabrication shop workAWS D1.1Structural welding on the terminals and plants is built to it, and it suits a shop-based inspector.
Gas pipelines, compressor stations, tie-insAPI 1104Federal pipeline rules incorporate it for welding and acceptance.
Bridge steel for state highway workAWS D1.5The bridge welding code used for state transportation steel.

LNG storage tanks are built to API tank standards that are not Part C options, so tank inspectors usually pick between the ASME book and D1.1 depending on where the rest of their experience lies. Study the edition AWS names on your application, which can be older than the newest printing. Background reading: AWS D1.1, API 1104, ASME Section IX, ASME B31.3 and AWS D1.5.

AWS sections around Lake Charles

AWS organizes its members into local sections. South Louisiana has several, including the Acadiana Section to the east and the Baton Rouge and New Orleans sections, which sit in AWS District 9; the AWS section finder shows which one meets nearest to you in Calcasieu Parish.

For a CWI candidate, a section is more useful than it first appears. Meetings put you in a room with QC managers, welding engineers and working inspectors who know which code book local contractors prefer, how they got ready for the practical, and which projects are hiring. They are also where you find supervisors willing to confirm your welding history when AWS asks for verifiable experience. Current officers and meeting places are listed through the section finder on aws.org.

Where Lake Charles welders learn the trade

SOWELA Technical Community College in Lake Charles runs a welding technology certificate, and the college has added short programs when industry needed them: it once ran a compressed evening welding course at its Morgan Smith campus in Jennings with Leevac Shipyards to fill shipyard jobs, and it has offered free pipefitting training. Bechtel has also funded free pipefitting courses and workforce readiness training for local residents as Louisiana LNG ramps up. Union apprenticeships and contractor craft programs train many of the pipe welders the plants depend on.

Those routes matter twice for the CWI. AWS lets completed trade or vocational courses reduce the experience it requires, from five years with a high school diploma alone to four. And a school transcript or apprenticeship record makes it far easier to document the welding-related work you list on the application. SOWELA and the other programs mentioned here have no connection with the Atlantis course; they are simply where much of the local workforce starts.

Booking the CWI exam from Lake Charles

Apply to AWS first. Once AWS accepts the application it sends a confirmation letter carrying an eligibility code, and that code lets you book the two computer-based papers with Prometric: Part A, 150 fundamentals questions, and Part C, the open-book code paper of roughly 50 to 65 questions. AWS says Prometric has more than 100 test centers in the United States, so you can choose the one that suits your travel. Part B is different. AWS runs the practical itself, with tools and specimens it supplies plus 46 questions, and only at its seminar and examination locations on dates it sets. That may mean a drive to Houston or to another Gulf Coast city where AWS holds a session, so check the AWS schedule before committing to dates. You need at least 72% on each part.

AWS publishes its examination and seminar fees on aws.org. The CWI exam budget guide helps you add travel and time off to that figure, and the part-by-part breakdown shows where candidates tend to lose marks.

Studying around construction rotations, turnarounds and storm season

Lake Charles work rarely leaves a tidy study window. Large LNG builds run long shifts with heavy overtime, refinery and chemical turnarounds pull crews into weeks of twelve-hour days, and the Atlantic hurricane season, from June to November, can turn a quiet month into a repair surge. After Hurricane Laura in 2020, refineries and chemical plants around the city stayed down for a period while damage was assessed and repaired.

The online format is built for that kind of year. Work through the fundamentals during a slower stretch, keep your code book in the truck and look up the clause that governs the joints you see each day, practise Part B measurements on scrap coupons and cut-outs, and save the timed papers for the run-up to your Prometric appointment. Questions go to the instructor in writing whenever they come up, night shift included. Candidates who would rather have a fixed structure can book one-to-one sessions around their days off.

Corporate: six days at a Lake Charles-area contractor, plant or shop

An employer with a group to prepare can have all six days delivered at its own facility in the Lake Charles area. Groups here are often mixed: an LNG contractor might send piping inspectors toward the ASME book and structural inspectors toward D1.1, so the code day is split by book. The practical day uses the company's own fillet gauges, bridge cam gauges, hi-lo gauges and real welds, such as stainless spool cut-outs or welder test coupons, so the measuring practice matches what those people will accept on the job. Dates can be planned around turnarounds, module deliveries or commissioning milestones. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally; an employer cannot submit the application, the experience record or the vision examination on anyone's behalf.

One-to-one: online or in person

Some candidates do better with a tutor than with a study plan. A QC lead returning to exams after many years, a welding supervisor who needs the credential for a new role, or someone who fell short on one part and wants to target it can book six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor. Sessions run online, or in person at a location agreed when you book. The six-day outline stays the same; the time is weighted toward your weak areas and your chosen code book.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS ties the experience requirement to education. A high school diploma means five years of welding-related work, a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology cuts that to one, completed vocational training sits at four, and less schooling raises it. The full table is on the national CWI course page, and AWS has the final word on what counts as welding-related. You also need the AWS Visual Acuity Record: near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, plus a color perception test, done by a qualified practitioner and recent enough for your exam date. Contract hands who have moved between plants should start listing every job, with dates, contractor, site, processes, codes and a supervisor contact, well before applying. If you do not yet have the years, the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) credential lets you inspect under a CWI while you build them. The CWI requirements and career guide covers the detail.

After the CWI: Lake Charles career paths

AWS keeps a CWI valid for nine years, with renewal paperwork due at the third and sixth years and recertification at nine. In Southwest Louisiana the next move usually follows the sector. LNG and refinery inspectors often grow into lead QC roles and later the AWS Senior Certified Welding Inspector (SCWI); see the Senior CWI pathway. Some add AWS endorsements for further codes. Plant inspectors frequently look at API 510 or API 570, which API runs under its own rules and which Atlantis does not train for.

Many add nondestructive testing so they can carry out visual, magnetic particle, penetrant or ultrasonic examinations themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its NDT staff once training and method experience are in place, and Atlantis provides that training: see NDT training in Lake Charles, VT Level 2, UT Level 2 and the CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II comparison. For hands-on rehearsal between plant shifts, the Practical NDT welding workshop simulator walks through inspection steps on a laptop. For the inspection side, see visual testing, weld inspection and ultrasonic testing in Lake Charles.

Other Gulf Coast CWI pages, and a quote

Candidates across the region can compare CWI exam prep in Houston, Beaumont, Baton Rouge and New Orleans.

For a quote, tell us how many people are preparing, which format suits each one (corporate, online or one-to-one), the code book each plans to use, and a short summary of their schooling and welding history. For delivery at your site, add the location, the gauges and sample welds you can provide, and any turnaround or commissioning dates to avoid. Atlantis does not publish course fees and gives a quote on request through the Lake Charles CWI quote request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Lake Charles?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Lake Charles; the company's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. Individuals study online with an instructor answering questions, employers can have the six days delivered at their own facility, and single candidates can book one-to-one sessions online or in person. See the course outline.

The American Welding Society. AWS administers every part of the examination, checks eligibility and issues the CWI to those who pass. The Atlantis course is preparation for that exam, and AWS has not approved or endorsed it.

faq.q: I inspect LNG process piping. Which Part C code should I choose?
faq.a: Most piping inspectors on the terminals choose the ASME package, which pairs Section IX welding qualification with the B31.1 and B31.3 piping codes, because liquefaction train piping is built to B31.3. See ASME B31.3.

faq.q: I work on pipe racks and module frames. Which book fits?
faq.a: AWS D1.1, the structural steel code, is the usual choice for module, rack and steel support work and for shop-based inspectors. Pipeline and compressor station inspectors are better served by API 1104.

faq.q: Where do Lake Charles candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Fundamentals and Code Application are computer-based tests booked at a Prometric center with the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter. The practical is run by AWS at its own seminar and examination locations on set dates, which can mean travelling to Houston or another Gulf Coast city.

faq.q: Can an LNG contractor have the six days delivered on its site?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to the employer's facility, uses its gauges and real welds, and splits the code day between ASME and D1.1 groups where needed. Each person still applies to AWS individually. Request a quote.

faq.q: Can I do the one-to-one option in person?
faq.a: Yes. A Lake Charles candidate who books one-to-one gets six days of sessions with the instructor alone, either online or face to face at a place agreed at booking. It is never a public class.

faq.q: Are the practice questions taken from the AWS exam?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes every practice question to the topic areas AWS publishes, and it has no access to the examination or its question bank.

faq.q: Does a SOWELA welding certificate reduce the experience I need?
faq.a: It may. AWS treats completed trade or vocational courses as education that lowers the requirement from five years to four, but AWS alone decides which education row your credential falls into. SOWELA is not connected with the Atlantis course.

faq.q: What NDT training can I add after the CWI?
faq.a: Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT, after which your employer certifies you under its written practice. See NDT training in Lake Charles.
